column1: psql - list tables, and describe one table's structure (columns/indexes/FKs)?
column2:
\dt            list tables in the current schema
\d tablename   describe a table (columns, types, indexes, foreign keys)
\d+ tablename  same, more detail
Backslash commands take NO semicolon; SQL statements DO.

column1: psql - open a shell inside a Compose postgres container?
column2:
docker compose exec postgres psql -U "$POSTGRES_USER" -d "$POSTGRES_DB"
# -U user, -d database. Prompt becomes  dbname=#

column1: psql - core meta-commands: list DBs, switch DB, list schemas, quit, expanded rows?
column2:
\l         list databases
\c db      connect to (switch) a database
\dn        list schemas
\x         toggle expanded display (key/value rows - good for wide tables)
\q         quit
\?         help for backslash commands

column1: psql - the two rules that trip you up (semicolon, schema scope, case)?
column2:
Backslash commands (\dt) take NO semicolon; SQL (SELECT ...) NEEDS one.
\dt shows only the CURRENT schema - use \dt *.* for all.
Names case-fold to lowercase unless double-quoted: \d "Users" for a capitalized name.

column1: Postgres - restore tables from a pg_dump .sql backup into a running Compose container?
column2:
cat backup.sql | docker compose exec -T postgres psql -U "$POSTGRES_USER" -d "$POSTGRES_DB"
-T disables TTY allocation (required when piping stdin).
The pg_dump .sql is plain SQL (CREATE TABLE + INSERTs), so psql just replays it.
Verify with \dt afterward.

column1: Postgres - dump just specific tables to a SQL file (backup before a drop)?
column2:
pg_dump -U "$POSTGRES_USER" -d "$POSTGRES_DB" -t table_a -t table_b > backup_$(date +%F).sql
# -t = restrict to a table (repeatable). In Compose: docker compose exec -T postgres pg_dump ...
